text.p: Swedish miner Trelleborg AB on Friday posted a worse-than-expected profit for the first nine months of 1996 and forecast a low full year figure which analysts attributed to less successful hedging.

Trelleborg reported a profit after financial items of 837 million crowns ($127 million) compared with 3.17 billion crowns a year ago although this did include 1.96 billion crown from the sale of shares in Falconbridge Ltd.
"The result was disappointing, especially the mining part of the company," said analyst Claes Vikbladh from Ohman.
The market had expected Trelleborg to post a profit of 891 million crowns. The share price dipped after the report was released by 1.5 crowns to 85.50 but recovered by the close.

But analysts said it was even more disappointing to see the company forecasting a lower-than-expected figure for calendar 1996, and saw 1997 staying flat. Most expected to keep Trelleborg on a hold trading recommendation.

"For the fourth quarter, earnings of the same order as for the third quarter are anticipated which means full-year earnings before taxes of about one billion crowns," Trelleborg's chief executive Kjell Nilsson said in a report for the nine months to September 30.
Analysts had expected Trelleborg to report a full year profit of 1.18 billion crowns.
"A lot of people thought that hedging would make profits higher in 1996," Vikbladh told Reuters. "Most people will have to revise their forecasts downwards."

A London-based analyst, who did not want to be named, said the disappointment was due largely to the hedging performance and the falling copper price on which Trelleborg's mining division is heavily dependent.
"Before Trelleborg has been very successful in hedging, especially copper futures, so they have had good average prices in their portfolio," he said.
However unlike many Swedish companies reporting their earnings for the first nine months of 1996, Trelleborg did not report a loss from the appreciation in the crown.
"The effects of fluctuations in exchange rates were balanced by hedging," the company said.
Over the nine months Trelleborg reported a fall in sales to 15.29 billion crowns from 15.82 billion a year ago from its three business groups.
The only sector to report a rise was the rubber products unit where sales rose to 3.39 billion crowns from 3.34 billion even though volumes fell a little in the third quarter.
"They are quite aggressively building up the rubber area so this could peform better in 1997," said one analyst.

Sales for the mines and metals unit tumbled to 5.99 billion crowns from 6.34 billion "mainly as a result of volume and price falls for copper and copper-based manufactures on the markets in Central Europe", the company said.
"For other parts it was possible to compensate the effects of lower metal prices with increased volumes as a result of implemented capacity increases."
The distribution division saw sales slip to 5.45 billion from 6.07 billion due to lower prices and volumes falls.
"Really the result was disappointing in all areas," said a Stockholm-based analyst.
($1=6.59 crowns)
